To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The communication cost and communication time objective functions are incomparable; (ii) The communication cost algorithm outperforms the lower bound, while the communication time algorithm performs within a small constant factor from the lower bound.

(1) the communication cost of a data-item can be reduced by dynamically moving the replication scheme of this item towards a replication scheme where the data-item is stored on a minimum number of processors; (2) the communication time of a data-item, defined as the time it takes to read this item, can be reduced by moving the replication scheme towards a replication scheme in which the number of processors at which a data-item is replicated is equal to the number of processors which read this data-item;

(i) there exists a dynamic replication algorithm for minimizing the communication cost that achieves a performance within an additive constant of the lower bound, (ii) there does not exist a dynamic replication algorithm that minimizes the communication time, and achieves a performance within a constant factor of the lower bound.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (a) What are the best replication schemes for a data-item?
the following questions: (1) How to dynamically replicate data in a network so as to minimize communication cost?
the following questions: How to design a dynamic replication algorithm that optimizes the communication costs or communication time of a data-item.

the communication cost algorithm performs as good as the communication time algorithm, but is much more efficient in terms of communication and computation cost, and that the lower bound for dynamic replication is tight.

The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic replication is possible, and can be done with low overhead.
the performance of dynamic replication is very sensitive to the read-write pattern and that the communication cost and the communication time can be optimized simultaneously.

the optimal replication scheme for a dynamic read-write pattern is a function of the pattern, and that the performance of the optimal replication scheme depends only on the read-write pattern and not on the network topology.
